newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss minister says gold to be sold cautiously.
newsitem.headline: Swiss minister says gold to be sold cautiously.

text.p: Switzerland's finance minister reiterated on Tuesday that proposed sales of official gold reserves to finance a humanitarian foundation would be done cautiously to ensure they did not disrupt the market.

"We have to realise this (sale) very subtly over a long period of time so that the gold price would not be significantly affected," Finance Minister Kaspar Villiger told parliament during a debate about the country's role in World War Two.

Berne plans to revalue the country's 2,600 tonnes of gold reserves -- now on the Swiss National Bank's books at around a quarter of its market value -- at 60 percent of the market price, boosting their value by 14 billion Swiss francs. It would transfer seven billion in revalued gold to the foundation.

"This gold, lying unmanaged in the cellar, must of course be converted cautiously into securities and after a few years -- I stress not immediately, but after a few years -- would make available around 350 million a year in interest that could finance the foundation's humanitarian activities," he said.

The plan must still be approved by the legislature and faces a referendum next year. Populist politicians have said they will try to block the plan, which original opinion polls show most Swiss support.
The fate of the other seven billion in revalued gold remains unclear. Villiger said it was not necessary to decide this soon. --Zurich newsroom +41 1 631 7340
